questions.q: What is the difference between authentication and authorization?
options: Authentication proves who you are; authorization determines what that identity is allowed to do
They are two names for exactly the same process
Authorization happens before authentication in every case
Authentication only applies to service identities, never to users
questions.explain: Microsoft Entra ID (Lesson 9) handles authentication. RBAC handles the separate question of authorization.

questions.q: What are the three parts of every RBAC role assignment?
options: Who (a user, group, or service), what role, and at what scope
A username, a password, and a security question
A subscription, a region, and a resource group only
A budget, an alert threshold, and a tag
questions.explain: Every role assignment is who + what role + at what scope — subscription, resource group, or a single resource.

questions.q: Why does assigning "Contributor" at a resource group scope behave differently than assigning it at a subscription scope?
options: Scope controls how far a role's reach extends — subscription-level reaches every resource group beneath it, while resource-group-level is contained to that one group
There is no difference — Contributor always applies to the entire subscription
Resource group scope grants more permissions than subscription scope
Scope only affects billing, never actual permissions
questions.explain: The same role name means a different blast radius depending on where it's assigned.

questions.q: What does the principle of least privilege mean in practice?
options: Granting an identity only the access it actually needs to do its job, not more just in case
Giving every identity Owner access so nothing is ever blocked
Removing all access from every identity by default and never granting any
Only applying RBAC to service identities, never to human users
questions.explain: A reporting analyst who only views cost data gets Reader at the resource group scope, not Owner at the subscription scope.

questions.q: A billing clerk and a database administrator both sign in successfully with Entra ID. What does that success alone tell you?
options: Only that both identities were authenticated — it says nothing about what either one is authorized to do
That both identities automatically have identical permissions
That both identities have Owner access at the subscription scope
That RBAC is not needed for either identity
questions.explain: Authentication and authorization are separate questions; successful sign-in only answers the first one.
